# Absolute Galois group

*Image: Complex conjugate picture.svg.* The absolute Galois group of the [real numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_numbers) is a [cyclic group](wikipedia://en/52327) of order 2 generated by complex conjugation, since $\mathbb{C}$ is the separable closure of $\mathbb{R}$ and $[\mathbb{C}:\mathbb{R}]=2$.

::: {#o1 .subject cue=lead name="Absolute Galois group"}

In [mathematics](wikipedia://en/18831), particularly in [anabelian geometry](wikipedia://en/27119265) and [$p$-adic](wikipedia://en/51423) geometry, the **absolute Galois group** $G_K$ of a [field](wikipedia://en/10603) $K$ is the [Galois group](wikipedia://en/12673) of $K^\textrm{sep}$ over $K$, where $K^\textrm{sep}$ is a [separable closure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Separable_closure) of $K$. Alternatively, it is the group of all [automorphisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automorphisms) of the [algebraic closure](wikipedia://en/3129) of $K$ that fix $K$. The absolute Galois group is well-defined [up to](wikipedia://en/44787) [inner automorphism](wikipedia://en/61839). It is a [profinite group](wikipedia://en/24266).

:::

When $K$ is a [perfect field](wikipedia://en/505088), $K^\textrm{sep}$ is the same as an [algebraic closure](wikipedia://en/3129) $K^\textrm{alg}$ of $K$. Notably, this holds when $K$ has [characteristic zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Characteristic_zero) or is [finite](wikipedia://en/11615).

::: {#o3 .example cue=heading name="Examples"}

## Examples {#Examples}

- The absolute Galois group of an algebraically closed field is [trivial](wikipedia://en/193059).
- The absolute Galois group of the [real numbers](wikipedia://en/20646438) is a cyclic group of two elements ([complex conjugation](wikipedia://en/173918) and the identity map), since $\mathbb{C}$ is the separable closure of $\mathbb{R}$, and its [degree](wikipedia://en/4382697) over $\mathbb{R}$ is $[\mathbb{C}:\mathbb{R}]=2$.
- The absolute Galois group of a [finite field](wikipedia://en/11615) $K$ is isomorphic to the group of [profinite integers](wikipedia://en/46531203)

$\hat{\mathbb{Z}} = \varprojlim \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}.$[^o4]

The [Frobenius automorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frobenius_automorphism) is a canonical (topological) generator of $G_K$. If $K$ has $q$ elements, the map is given by $x\mapsto x^q$ for all $x$ in $K^\textrm{alg}$.

- The absolute Galois group of the [field of rational functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_of_rational_functions) with complex coefficients is free (as a profinite group). This result is due to [Adrien Douady](wikipedia://en/1604604) and has its origins in [Riemann's existence theorem](wikipedia://en/78698035).[^o5]
- More generally, let $C$ be an algebraically closed field and $x$ an indeterminate. Then the absolute Galois group of $C(x)$ is free of rank equal to the cardinality of $C$. This result is due to [David Harbater](wikipedia://en/3521313) and [Florian Pop](wikipedia://en/24789740), and was also proved later by Dan Haran and [Moshe Jarden](wikipedia://en/48527380) using algebraic methods.[^o6][^o7][^o8]
- Let $K$ be a [finite extension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finite_extension) of the [$p$-adic numbers](wikipedia://en/51423) $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For $p\neq 2$, its absolute Galois group is generated by $[K:\mathbb{Q}_p]+3$ elements and has an explicit description by generators and relations. This is a result of Uwe Jannsen and Kay Wingberg.[^o9][^o10] Some results are known in the case $p=2$, but the structure for $\mathbb{Q}_2$ is not known.[^o11]
- Another case in which the absolute Galois group has been determined is for the largest [totally real](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally_real) subfield of the field of [algebraic numbers](wikipedia://en/1158).[^o12]

:::

## Problems {#Problems}

- No direct description is known for the absolute Galois group of the [rational numbers](wikipedia://en/19727024). In this case, it follows from [Belyi's theorem](wikipedia://en/3144280) that the absolute Galois group has a faithful [action](wikipedia://en/12781) on the *[dessins d'enfants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dessins_d'enfants)* of [Grothendieck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck) (maps on surfaces), enabling us to "see" the Galois theory of [algebraic number fields](wikipedia://en/28730822). It is one of the goals of [anabelian geometry](wikipedia://en/27119265) to solve this problem
- Let $K$ be the maximal [abelian extension](wikipedia://en/174448) of the rational numbers. Then **Shafarevich's conjecture** asserts that the absolute Galois group of $K$ is a free profinite group.[^o14]
- An interesting problem is to settle [Ján Mináč](wikipedia://en/74607395) and Nguyên Duy Tân's conjecture about vanishing of $n$-Massey products for $n \geq 3$.[^o15][^o16]

## Some general results {#Some_general_results}

- The [Neukirch–Uchida theorem](wikipedia://en/42095155) asserts that every isomorphism of the absolute Galois groups of algebraic number fields arises from a field automorphism. In particular, two absolute Galois groups of number fields are isomorphic if and only if the base fields are isomorphic.
- Every profinite group occurs as a Galois group of some [Galois extension](wikipedia://en/457064),[^o18] but not every profinite group occurs as an absolute Galois group. For example, the [Artin–Schreier theorem](wikipedia://en/1066093) asserts that if an absolute Galois group is finite, then it has order 1 or 2.
- Every [projective profinite group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projective_profinite_group) can be realized as an absolute Galois group of a [pseudo algebraically closed field](wikipedia://en/3696313). This result is due to [Alexander Lubotzky](wikipedia://en/22754130) and [Lou van den Dries](wikipedia://en/55143215).[^o19]

## Uses in the geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence {#Uses_in_the_geometrization_of_the_local_Langlands_correspondence}

In their 2022 paper on the geometrization of the [local Langlands correspondence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Langlands_correspondence), [Laurent Fargues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurent_Fargues) and [Peter Scholze](wikipedia://en/39409306) looked to recover information about a [local field](wikipedia://en/145375) *E* via its absolute Galois group, which is isomorphic to the [étale fundamental group](wikipedia://en/3022906) of Spec(*E*). This result was calculated while trying to evaluate the [Weil group](wikipedia://en/6375618) (which itself is a variant of the absolute Galois group) of *E*. This result arrives from the idea of the automorphism group *G*(*E*) of the trivial *G*-torsor over Spec(*E*); thus, *G*(*E*) relates to information over Spec(*E*), which is an anabelian question.[^o21]
